headline: Record fee and spread earnings drive a swing back to profit

kpis.label: GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders
Net Balance Sheet Value per share

summary_short: Apollo's Q2 2026 Adjusted Net Income rose 11% y/y to $1.31B ($2.11/share) on record Fee Related Earnings of $785M (+25% y/y) and Spread Related Earnings of $877M (+7% y/y); GAAP net income was $1.34B ($2.18/share basic), rebounding from Q1's tax-driven GAAP loss.
summary_long: Adjusted Net Income rose 11% y/y to $1.31B ($2.11/share, +10% y/y), driven by record Fee Related Earnings of $785M (+25% y/y, 120bp margin expansion) on higher management fees (Athora's PIC acquisition, Bridge, organic Athene growth) and record capital-solutions fees, plus Spread Related Earnings of $877M (+7% y/y) on organic Retirement Services growth. Total AUM reached $1.05 trillion (+25% y/y) on $60B of quarterly inflows; Fee-Generating AUM rose 34% to $858B. GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders was $1.34B ($2.18/share basic), rebounding from Q1's $(1.93)B GAAP loss caused by a one-time $1.7B Bermuda tax charge. Apollo repurchased $102M of stock and declared a $0.5625/share dividend. No forward guidance was issued in the release.

drivers.explanation: Growth in both segment earnings streams -- FRE and SRE -- plus continued fee and spread diversification; together FRE and SRE totaled $1.7 billion for the quarter.
Tracks ANI dollar growth; per-share growth trails ANI dollar growth slightly on a higher weighted-average diluted share count versus a year ago.

drivers.metric: GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders
drivers.explanation: Rebounds from Q1's loss, which stemmed from a $1.7 billion one-time tax charge tied to Bermuda revoking ACRA's Corporate Income Tax Act election; also benefited from $2,989M of investment-related gains this quarter versus a $2,078M loss in Q1.
Follows the net-income rebound described above; not further decomposed by the release.
Largely reflects a swing in investment-related gains (losses) to +$2,989M this quarter from -$2,078M in Q1 and -$5M a year ago, rather than underlying operating growth.

Record quarterly fee-related revenue plus positive operating leverage produced 120 basis points of margin expansion; management fees grew on Athora's PIC acquisition, Bridge, and organic Athene growth.
Strong and diversified organic growth trends and improving net spread; included a 9% return on Athene's alternative portfolio versus management's 11% long-term expectation.
Driven by $60 billion of quarterly inflows and $298 billion over the last twelve months, plus mark-to-market appreciation, partly offset by Athene run-off outflows.
Asset Management contributed $225 billion of inflows including Athora's PIC acquisition; Retirement Services contributed $78 billion of gross inflows from organic Athene growth.

drivers.metric: Net Balance Sheet Value per share
drivers.explanation: Not explained in the release beyond the underlying net-income and balance-sheet items disclosed elsewhere.
CEO Marc Rowan cited record earnings across Asset Management and Retirement Services and positioned Apollo to benefit from private markets shifting toward greater transparency, liquidity, and access.

confidence_notes: Run in force-regenerate mode per instructions (Step-0 already-exists guard skipped and the run was treated as an overwrite from the start); in practice no prior summary file existed on disk for APO_US_FY2026_Q2.json, so this write does not actually overwrite prior data, but it followed the full force-regenerate procedure throughout. scripts/resolve-edgar-exhibit.mjs exited 'no EX-99* exhibit found' for this filing (accession 0001858681-26-000036 uses non-standard exhibit filenames erex9912q2026.htm and agmearningsrelease2q2026.htm rather than an 'ex99' pattern the script recognizes); the correct documents were identified manually from the script's own candidate listing -- the short erex9912q2026.htm is a brief dividend/webcast notice while agmearningsrelease2q2026.htm carries the actual financial tables, and both were fetched. The shard's eps_usd KPI ($2.11, source Yahoo earningsChart) is Apollo's own non-GAAP Adjusted Net Income (ANI) per share -- Apollo's stated primary earnings metric -- but the shard's prior_qq (-$3.27) and prior_yy ($1.00) values are SEC EDGAR GAAP Basic EPS, a different basis; per this repo's same-basis rule, the y/y and q/q deltas for ANI per share reported here were instead computed directly from the release's own ANI-per-share series ($1.92 in 2Q'25, $1.94 in 1Q'26, $2.11 in 2Q'26), not the resolver's cross-basis priors. Total revenues ($11,153M) and its y/y delta are dominated by non-operating 'Investment related gains (losses)' swings (+$2,989M this quarter vs -$5M a year ago and -$2,078M in Q1) under GAAP consolidation of Athene's investment portfolio -- not a measure of underlying operating growth; FRE and SRE are Apollo's own segment-earnings metrics and are cleaner growth signals. Q1 2026 GAAP net income included a one-time $1.7 billion tax expense from Bermuda's revocation of ACRA's election under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023, which explains most of the GAAP net-income and EPS swing between Q1 and Q2. No explicit forward guidance (revenue, EPS, or otherwise) was found in either fetched document.
